s0001.literal: Confucius said: "Of the sage's virtue, what can be added to filial piety!
s0001.idiomatic: Confucius said, "Of the sage's virtue, what can be added to filial piety!

s0002.literal: " Filial piety is the root of the hundred conduct, the utmost of human relations.
s0002.idiomatic: Filial piety is the root of the hundred conduct, the utmost of human relations.

s0003.literal: All who possess a sentient nature—who does not proceed from this?
s0003.idiomatic: All who possess a sentient nature—who does not proceed from this?

s0004.literal: As for fully sustaining life in nurture and fully mourning at the send-off, or weeping blood for three years and abstaining from gruel for seven days, thinking with the keen longing of "The Mugwort" and pursuing the deep grace of looking back in care, or virtue moving heaven and earth and sincerity penetrating the hidden and manifest—in every age, surely there have been such men.
s0004.idiomatic: Whether in fully sustaining life in nurture or fully mourning at the send-off, in weeping blood for three years or abstaining from gruel for seven days, in the keen longing of "The Mugwort" or the deep grace of a parent's watchful care, or in virtue that moves heaven and earth and sincerity that pierces the hidden and manifest—in every age there have surely been such men.

s0005.literal: Chen inherited Liang's age of mourning and turmoil; customs were dissolving and transformation grew thin, and when traces lay hidden in lanes and alleys they went unheard by sight or hearing. What is gathered here now is to supply what is lacking.
s0005.idiomatic: Chen inherited Liang's age of mourning and turmoil; customs dissolved and transformation grew thin, and when traces lay hidden in lanes and alleys they went unheard. What is gathered here is to supply what is lacking.

s0007.literal: Yin Buhai, styled Changqing, was a man of Changping in Chen commandery.
s0007.idiomatic: Yin Buhai, styled Changqing, was from Changping in Chen commandery.

s0008.literal: His grandfather Ren was a traveling aide to the Prince of Yuzhang of Qi.
s0008.idiomatic: His grandfather Ren was a traveling aide to the Prince of Yuzhang of Qi.

s0009.literal: His father Gaoming was a Liang director of the central arms bureau in the Secretariat.
s0009.idiomatic: His father Gaoming was a Liang director of the central arms bureau in the Secretariat.

s0010.literal: Buhai was by nature supremely filial; in his father's mourning he exceeded the rites, and from this he first won a name.
s0010.idiomatic: Buhai was by nature supremely filial; in mourning his father he exceeded the rites, and from this he first won a name.

s0011.literal: His family for generations was frugal; their dwelling was very poor. He had five younger brothers, all still young and weak. Buhai served his aged mother and reared his young brothers, toiling at every task without limit, and the scholar-officials praised him for his earnest conduct.
s0011.idiomatic: His family for generations was frugal and their dwelling very poor. He had five younger brothers, all still young. Buhai served his aged mother and reared his young brothers, toiling at every task without limit, and scholar-officials praised his earnest conduct.

s0012.literal: At seventeen he entered Liang service as an assistant in the Court Tribunal.
s0012.idiomatic: At seventeen he entered Liang service as an assistant in the Court Tribunal.

s0013.literal: Buhai excelled at governmental affairs and additionally adorned himself with Confucian learning. Where statutes and punishments had weights and measures that were inconvenient, he would submit a memorial on them, and many were adopted.
s0013.idiomatic: Buhai excelled at governmental affairs and additionally adorned himself with Confucian learning. Where statutes and punishments had weights and measures that were inconvenient, he would submit a memorial, and many were adopted.

s0014.literal: In the fifth year of Datong he was moved to recorder of the staff in the Pacify-West establishment, and soon held his original post concurrently as communicating affairs attendant of the Eastern Palace.
s0014.idiomatic: In Datong year 5 (539) he was moved to recorder of the staff in the Pacify-West establishment, and soon held his original post concurrently as communicating affairs attendant of the eastern palace.

s0015.literal: At that time many court and government affairs were entrusted to the Eastern Palace. Buhai with the attendant Yu Jianwu attended on the days of direct audience to report affairs. Emperor Wu of Liang once told Jianwu: "You are a man of letters; clerical business is not your strength—why not have Yin Buhai come instead?
s0015.idiomatic: At that time many court and government affairs were entrusted to the eastern palace. Buhai and attendant Yu Jianwu attended on the days of direct audience to report affairs. Emperor Wu of Liang once told Jianwu, "You are a man of letters; clerical business is not your strength—why not have Yin Buhai come instead?

s0016.literal: " He was known and valued to this degree.
s0016.idiomatic: He was known and valued to this degree.

s0017.literal: Emperor Jianwen of Liang also, because Buhai was skilled at serving his parents, bestowed on his mother the Lady Cai brocade skirts and jackets, felt mats, quilts, and bedding, single and double layers all complete.
s0017.idiomatic: Emperor Jianwen of Liang also, because Buhai was skilled at serving his parents, bestowed on his mother Lady Cai brocade skirts and jackets, felt mats, quilts, and bedding, single and double layers all complete.

s0018.literal: In the seventh year he was made footsoldiers commandant of the Eastern Palace.
s0018.idiomatic: In year 7 he was made footsoldiers commandant of the eastern palace.

s0019.literal: At the beginning of Taiqing he was moved to staff adviser of the Pacify-North establishment, his attendant post remaining as before.
s0019.idiomatic: At the start of Taiqing (547) he was moved to staff adviser of the Pacify-North establishment, his attendant post remaining as before.

s0020.literal: In Hou Jing's rebellion Buhai followed Emperor Jianwen of Liang into the Inner City.
s0020.idiomatic: In Hou Jing's rebellion Buhai followed Emperor Jianwen of Liang into the Inner City.

s0021.literal: When the Inner City fell, Emperor Jianwen was in the Secretariat. Jing, in armor and leading troops, entered court for audience at the steps and passed by to pay respects to Emperor Jianwen.
s0021.idiomatic: When the Inner City fell, Emperor Jianwen was in the Secretariat. Jing, in armor and leading troops, entered court for audience at the steps and passed by to pay respects to Emperor Jianwen.

s0022.literal: Jing's soldiers were all mixed breeds of Qiang and Hu; they charged left and right, very insolent. The guards did not startle or give way—only Buhai and palace attendant Xu Chi stood at the side unmoved.
s0022.idiomatic: Jing's soldiers were all mixed breeds of Qiang and Hu; they charged left and right, very insolent. The guards did not startle or give way—only Buhai and palace attendant Xu Chi stood at the side unmoved.

s0023.literal: When Emperor Jianwen was confined by Jing, he sent someone to request that Buhai dwell with him; Jing assented, and Buhai waited on him with ever greater care.
s0023.idiomatic: When Emperor Jianwen was confined by Jing, he sent someone to request that Buhai dwell with him; Jing assented, and Buhai waited on him with ever greater care.

s0024.literal: Emperor Jianwen one night dreamed he swallowed a clod of earth and was very displeased. He told Buhai, and Buhai said: "In old times Duke Wen of Jin went into exile; a rustic gave him a clod, and in the end he returned to Jin. Your Majesty's dream—does the matter match this?
s0024.idiomatic: Emperor Jianwen one night dreamed he swallowed a clod of earth and was very displeased. He told Buhai, and Buhai said, "In old times Duke Wen of Jin went into exile; a rustic gave him a clod, and in the end he returned to Jin. Your Majesty's dream—does the matter match this?

s0025.literal: " Emperor Jianwen said: "If Heaven sends a sign, I hope these words are not in vain."
s0025.idiomatic: Emperor Jianwen said, "If Heaven sends a sign, I hope these words are not in vain."

s0026.literal: When Emperor Yuan of Liang took the throne, he made Buhai a Secretariat gentleman and concurrently director of the Court Tribunal, and thus led his household west.
s0026.idiomatic: When Emperor Yuan of Liang took the throne, he made Buhai a Secretariat gentleman and concurrently director of the Court Tribunal, and thus led his household west.

s0027.literal: At the fall of Jiangling, Buhai was first at another place directing battle and lost track of where his mother was.
s0027.idiomatic: At the fall of Jiangling, Buhai was first at another place directing battle and lost track of where his mother was.

s0028.literal: The season was bitterly cold; ice and snow fell together, and the old and weak who had frozen to death filled ditches and moats. Buhai walked the roads weeping and searched near and far, going everywhere. Whenever he came upon a corpse in a ditch or stream he threw himself down, lifted and examined the body; his whole person was frozen and soaked. He took no food or drink, and his cries never ceased. After seven days thus he found his mother's corpse.
s0028.idiomatic: The season was bitterly cold; ice and snow fell together, and the old and weak who had frozen to death filled ditches and moats. Buhai walked the roads weeping and searched near and far without rest. Whenever he came upon a corpse in a ditch or stream he threw himself down, lifted and examined the body, his whole person frozen and soaked. He took no food or drink, and his cries never ceased. After seven days thus he found his mother's corpse.

s0029.literal: Buhai leaned on the corpse and wept; each time he raised his voice he would lose breath. Passersby on the road none but shed tears for him.
s0029.idiomatic: Buhai leaned on the corpse and wept; each time he raised his voice he would lose breath. Every passerby on the road shed tears for him.

s0030.literal: He then had a temporary burial at Jiangling and, with Wang Pou and Yu Xin, together entered Chang'an. From then on he ate vegetables and wore plain cloth, wasted to bone standing alone; all who saw him were moved to pity.
s0030.idiomatic: He then had a temporary burial at Jiangling and, with Wang Pou and Yu Xin, together entered Chang'an. From then on he ate vegetables and wore plain cloth, wasted to bone standing alone; all who saw him were moved to pity.

s0032.literal: Buniu, styled Jiqing, was Buhai's younger brother.
s0032.idiomatic: Buniu, styled Jiqing, was Buhai's younger brother.

s0033.literal: In youth he established a reputation for integrity; in his father's mourning he was famed for supreme filial piety.
s0033.idiomatic: In youth he established a reputation for integrity; in mourning his father he was famed for supreme filial piety.

s0034.literal: He loved reading and especially excelled at the arts of office. Entering Liang service he began as director of the central arms bureau in the Secretariat and was greatly praised for ability.
s0034.idiomatic: He loved reading and especially excelled at the arts of office. Entering Liang service he began as director of the central arms bureau in the Secretariat and was greatly praised for ability.

s0035.literal: When Emperor Yuan of Liang assumed the regency, he was appointed martial-proclamation general and staff adviser to the Prince of Wuling.
s0035.idiomatic: When Emperor Yuan of Liang assumed the regency, he was appointed martial-proclamation general and staff adviser to the Prince of Wuling.

s0036.literal: At the beginning of Chengsheng he was moved to magistrate of Wukang.
s0036.idiomatic: At the start of Chengsheng (552) he was moved to magistrate of Wukang.

s0037.literal: At the time arms and famine ravaged the land and the people drifted in flight. Buniu toured to comfort and gather them in, and those who came swaddled on the back numbered in the thousands.
s0037.idiomatic: At the time arms and famine ravaged the land and the people drifted in flight. Buniu toured to comfort and gather them in, and those who came swaddled on the back numbered in the thousands.

s0038.literal: It happened that Jiangling fell and his mother died; roads were cut off and for long he could not hurry to the funeral. Within four years he wept and cried day and night; in dwelling, food, and drink he constantly kept the rites of mourning.
s0038.idiomatic: It happened that Jiangling fell and his mother died; roads were cut off and for long he could not hurry to the funeral. Within four years he wept and cried day and night; in dwelling, food, and drink he constantly kept the rites of mourning.

s0039.literal: When the Founder received the abdication, he was summoned as martial-proclamation general and made magistrate of Lou.
s0039.idiomatic: When the Founder received the abdication, he was summoned as martial-proclamation general and made magistrate of Lou.

s0040.literal: By then his fourth elder brother Buqi had first gone to Jiangling and brought back their mother's coffin for burial.
s0040.idiomatic: By then his fourth elder brother Buqi had first gone to Jiangling and brought back their mother's coffin for burial.

s0041.literal: Buniu's observances in dwelling were as at the first news of bereavement; he did so for another three years.
s0041.idiomatic: Buniu's observances in dwelling were as at the first news of bereavement; he did so for another three years.

s0042.literal: He himself carried earth and with his hands planted pine and cypress. At each year's seasonal sacrifices at the solstices he would fast for three days without eating.
s0042.idiomatic: He himself carried earth and with his hands planted pine and cypress. At each year's seasonal sacrifices at the solstices he would fast for three days without eating.

s0043.literal: When Emperor Wen took the throne, he was made director of the left bureau for the people in the Secretariat but did not accept; later he was made staff adviser to the Prince of Shixing and concurrently right vice director in the Secretariat, then moved to communicating affairs attendant of the Eastern Palace.
s0043.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen took the throne, he was made director of the left bureau for the people in the Secretariat but did not accept; later he was made staff adviser to the Prince of Shixing and concurrently right vice director in the Secretariat, then moved to communicating affairs attendant of the eastern palace.

s0044.literal: When Emperor Wen died, the Deposed Emperor succeeded; Emperor Xuan was Grand Tutor and recorded affairs of the Secretariat to assist in government, and was greatly where court expectation turned.
s0044.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen died, the Deposed Emperor succeeded; Emperor Xuan was grand tutor and recorded affairs of the Secretariat to assist in government, and was greatly where court expectation turned.

s0045.literal: Buniu had always stood on his reputation for integrity and had again been entrusted by the Eastern Palace. He therefore joined Vice Director Dao Zhongju, Secretariat attendant Liu Shizhi, right vice director Wang Xian, and others in plotting to forge an edict removing Emperor Xuan.
s0045.idiomatic: Buniu had always stood on his reputation for integrity and had again been entrusted by the eastern palace. He therefore joined vice director Dao Zhongju, Secretariat attendant Liu Shizhi, right vice director Wang Xian, and others in plotting to forge an edict removing Emperor Xuan.

s0046.literal: The crowd hesitated and did not dare act first; Buniu then galloped to the chief minister's residence and in person proclaimed the edict, ordering the prince regent to return to his mansion.
s0046.idiomatic: The crowd hesitated and did not dare act first; Buniu then galloped to the chief minister's residence and in person proclaimed the edict, ordering the prince regent to return to his mansion.

s0047.literal: When the affair broke, Zhongju and the rest were all executed. Emperor Xuan had long valued Buniu and specially pardoned him, merely stripping his office.
s0047.idiomatic: When the affair broke, Zhongju and the rest were all executed. Emperor Xuan had long valued Buniu and specially pardoned him, merely stripping his office.

s0048.literal: When Emperor Xuan took the throne, he was made staff adviser and military strategist to the Prince of Shixing, with the additional rank of recruit-the-distance general.
s0048.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuan took the throne, he was made staff adviser and military strategist to the Prince of Shixing, with the additional rank of recruit-the-distance general.

s0049.literal: Soon he was made grand master of works but did not accept the appointment; he was additionally made irregular attendant of the scattered cavalry and again concurrently right vice director in the Secretariat.
s0049.idiomatic: Soon he was made grand master of works but did not accept the appointment; he was additionally made irregular attendant of the scattered cavalry and again concurrently right vice director in the Secretariat.

s0050.literal: Shortly he was moved to direct and upright attendant of the scattered cavalry, his vice directorship remaining as before.
s0050.idiomatic: Shortly he was moved to direct and upright attendant of the scattered cavalry, his vice directorship remaining as before.

s0051.literal: In the fifth year of Taijian he died, aged fifty-six.
s0051.idiomatic: In Taijian year 5 (573) he died, aged fifty-six.

s0052.literal: An edict posthumously made him director of the Secretariat.
s0052.idiomatic: An edict posthumously made him director of the Secretariat.

s0053.literal: His third elder brother Buyi, next Buzhan, next Buqi—all died young.
s0053.idiomatic: His third elder brother Buyi, next Buzhan, next Buqi—all died young.

s0054.literal: Buniu was the youngest. He served his second elder brother's widow, the Lady Zhang, with great care; the salary he received never entered his private quarters.
s0054.idiomatic: Buniu was the youngest. He served his second elder brother's widow Lady Zhang with great care; the salary he received never entered his private quarters.

s0055.literal: His eldest son Fantong rose to director of the gold bureau in the Secretariat.
s0055.idiomatic: His eldest son Fantong rose to director of the gold bureau in the Secretariat.

s0056.literal: Xie Zhen, styled Yuanzheng, was a man of Yangxia in Chen commandery, ninth-generation descendant of Jin Grand Tutor An.
s0056.idiomatic: Xie Zhen, styled Yuanzheng, was from Yangxia in Chen commandery, ninth-generation descendant of Jin grand tutor An.

s0057.literal: His grandfather Sui, Editorial footnote marker 1. was a Liang editorial assistant and crown prince attendant.
s0057.idiomatic: His grandfather Sui [1] served Liang as editorial assistant and crown prince attendant.

s0058.literal: His father Lin was a regular outside gentleman and concurrently irregular attendant of the scattered cavalry.
s0058.idiomatic: His father Lin was a regular outside gentleman and concurrently irregular attendant of the scattered cavalry.

s0059.literal: Zhen as a child was clever and keen, with a nature of utmost feeling.
s0059.idiomatic: Zhen as a child was clever and keen, with a nature of utmost feeling.

s0060.literal: His grandmother the Lady Ruan had long suffered from wind dizziness; whenever it flared she could not eat or drink for a day or two. Zhen was then seven years old; when his grandmother did not eat, Zhen also did not eat. Often it was so, and kin on both sides all marveled at him.
s0060.idiomatic: His grandmother Lady Ruan had long suffered from wind dizziness; whenever it flared she could not eat or drink for a day or two. Zhen was then seven; when his grandmother did not eat, Zhen also did not eat. Often it was so, and kin on both sides all marveled at him.

s0061.literal: His mother the Lady Wang taught Zhen the Analects and the Classic of Filial Piety; when he finished reading he could recite them.
s0061.idiomatic: His mother Lady Wang taught Zhen the Analects and the Classic of Filial Piety; when he finished reading he could recite them.

s0062.literal: At eight he once composed a five-character poem on spring days at leisure in retirement. His mother's brother, the Secretariat Director Wang Yun, marveled at its fine quality and told those close to him: "This boy can surely achieve great things. As for 'the wind has stilled yet flowers still fall'—that already follows in Hui Lian's steps.
s0062.idiomatic: At eight he once composed a five-character poem on spring days at leisure in retirement. His mother's brother, Secretariat director Wang Yun, marveled at its fine quality and told those close to him, "This boy can surely achieve great things. As for 'the wind has stilled yet flowers still fall'—that already follows in Hui Lian's steps.

s0063.literal: " From this men of reputation came to know him.
s0063.idiomatic: From this men of reputation came to know him.

s0064.literal: At thirteen he had broadly grasped the main purport of the Five Classics and especially excelled in the Zuo Tradition; he was skilled in cursive, clerical, seal, and insect scripts.
s0064.idiomatic: At thirteen he had broadly grasped the main purport of the Five Classics and especially excelled in the Zuo Tradition; he was skilled in cursive, clerical, seal, and insect scripts.

s0065.literal: At fourteen he suffered his father's mourning, collapsed to the ground crying, and several times lost breath and revived.
s0065.idiomatic: At fourteen he suffered his father's mourning, collapsed to the ground crying, and several times lost breath and revived.

s0066.literal: Earlier, his father Lin in mourning for his mother the Lady Ruan had not eaten and wept blood until he died. Family and guests feared Zhen would do the same. His father's younger brother Qia and his clansman Hao together went to Huayan Temple and asked the monk Long Claw to preach the law for Zhen, and also told Zhen: "A filial son has no brothers and must cherish himself utterly. If grief destroys your nature, who will nourish your mother?
s0066.idiomatic: Earlier, his father Lin in mourning for his mother Lady Ruan had not eaten and wept blood until he died. Family and guests feared Zhen would do the same. His father's younger brother Qia and his clansman Hao together went to Huayan Temple and asked the monk Long Claw to preach the law for Zhen, and also told Zhen, "A filial son has no brothers and must cherish himself utterly. If grief destroys your nature, who will nourish your mother?

s0067.literal: " After that he took a little thin gruel.
s0067.idiomatic: After that he took a little thin gruel.

s0068.literal: In the turmoil of Taiqing, kin scattered and fled. Zhen was lost in the fall of Jiangling; Hao fled in distress to Panyu, and Zhen's mother took the tonsure at Xuaming Temple.
s0068.idiomatic: In the turmoil of Taiqing, kin scattered and fled. Zhen was lost in the fall of Jiangling; Hao fled in distress to Panyu, and Zhen's mother took the tonsure at Xuaming Temple.

s0069.literal: When the Founder received the abdication, Hao returned to his home district and supported Zhen's mother for nearly twenty years.
s0069.idiomatic: When the Founder received the abdication, Hao returned to his home district and supported Zhen's mother for nearly twenty years.

s0070.literal: In the fifth year of Taijian Zhen then returned to court and was made outside arms officer on the staff of the Intelligent Martial establishment.
s0070.idiomatic: In Taijian year 5 (573) Zhen then returned to court and was made outside arms officer on the staff of the Intelligent Martial establishment.

s0071.literal: Shortly he was moved to director of the chariot bureau in the Secretariat, and soon moved to vice director.
s0071.idiomatic: Shortly he was moved to director of the chariot bureau in the Secretariat, and soon moved to vice director.

s0072.literal: When the Prince of Shixing Shuling was made inspector of Yangzhou, he brought in vice director of the rites bureau Ruan Zhuo as recorder of the staff and summoned Zhen as chief clerk; Zhen had no choice but to go.
s0072.idiomatic: When the Prince of Shixing Shuling was made inspector of Yangzhou, he brought in vice director of the rites bureau Ruan Zhuo as recorder of the staff and summoned Zhen as chief clerk; Zhen had no choice but to go.

s0073.literal: Soon he was moved to recorder of the staff and concurrently magistrate of Danyang.
s0073.idiomatic: Soon he was moved to recorder of the staff and concurrently magistrate of Danyang.

s0074.literal: Zhen judged that Shuling would harbor a rebellious intent and therefore, with Zhuo, kept themselves distant from the prince. Whenever there were feasts or outings he would plead illness and never take part. Shuling had long held him in esteem and did not blame him.
s0074.idiomatic: Zhen judged that Shuling would harbor a rebellious intent and therefore, with Zhuo, kept themselves distant from the prince. Whenever there were feasts or outings he would plead illness and never take part. Shuling had long held him in esteem and did not blame him.

s0075.literal: Shortly Emperor Xuan died and Shuling committed outrage; many staff members were implicated and seized—only Zhen and Zhuo were not charged.
s0075.idiomatic: Shortly Emperor Xuan died and Shuling committed outrage; many staff members were implicated and seized—only Zhen and Zhuo were not charged.

s0076.literal: Houzhu then ordered Zhen to enter and take charge of the inner palace records, moved him to friend of the Prince of Nanping, with the additional rank of recruit-the-distance general, in charge of recorder affairs.
s0076.idiomatic: Houzhu then ordered Zhen to enter and take charge of the inner palace records, moved him to friend of the Prince of Nanping, with the additional rank of recruit-the-distance general, in charge of recorder affairs.

s0077.literal: The establishment's chief recorder Zhou Que of Runan had newly been made director of the capital offenses bureau in the Secretariat and asked Zhen to draft his letter of declination; Houzhu read it and marveled.
s0077.idiomatic: The establishment's chief recorder Zhou Que of Runan had newly been made director of the capital offenses bureau in the Secretariat and asked Zhen to draft his letter of declination; Houzhu read it and marveled.

s0078.literal: Once at a banquet he asked Que: "Did you compose the memorial yourself?
s0078.idiomatic: Once at a banquet he asked Que, "Did you compose the memorial yourself?

s0079.literal: " Que replied: "Your servant's memorial was composed by Xie Zhen."
s0079.idiomatic: Que replied, "Your servant's memorial was composed by Xie Zhen."

s0080.literal: Houzhu thereupon ordered the attendant Wenqing Shi, Editorial footnote marker 2. [to say]: "Xie Zhen at the prince's establishment has no salary or rank; one hundred piculs of grain may be granted."
s0080.idiomatic: Houzhu thereupon ordered attendant Wenqing Shi [2], "Xie Zhen at the prince's establishment has no salary or rank; grant him one hundred piculs of grain."

s0081.literal: In the third year of Zhide he left office on his mother's mourning.
s0081.idiomatic: In Zhide year 3 (585) he left office on his mother's mourning.

s0082.literal: Shortly an edict recalled him to the establishment and again added recruit-the-distance general, in charge of the recorder's office.
s0082.idiomatic: Shortly an edict recalled him to the establishment and again added recruit-the-distance general, in charge of the recorder's office.

s0083.literal: Zhen repeatedly submitted memorials firmly declining. The edict in reply said: "I have read your memorial and take your meaning. Though I know your solitary grief lies in affliction, offices await the able and rites allow expedient suspension; you may force yourself despite illness and return to the establishment."
s0083.idiomatic: Zhen repeatedly submitted memorials firmly declining. The edict in reply said, "I have read your memorial and take your meaning. Though I know your solitary grief lies in affliction, offices await the able and rites allow expedient suspension; you may force yourself despite illness and return to the establishment."

s0084.literal: Zhen's mourning had wasted him to emaciation; in the end he could not go to the government offices.
s0084.idiomatic: Zhen's mourning had wasted him to emaciation; in the end he could not go to the government offices.

s0085.literal: At the time right vice director Xu Zuo and left vice director Shen Keqing of the Secretariat both came to visit Zhen. Seeing his frame wasted to bone standing alone, Zuo and the rest sighed in sorrow. Xu admonished him: "Brother, your years are already advanced; rites have a constant measure—you should slightly restrain your cutting grief and preserve yourself."
s0085.idiomatic: At the time right vice director Xu Zuo and left vice director Shen Keqing of the Secretariat both came to visit Zhen. Seeing his frame wasted to bone standing alone, Zuo and the rest sighed in sorrow. Xu admonished him, "Brother, your years are already advanced; rites have a constant measure—you should slightly restrain your cutting grief and preserve yourself."

s0086.literal: Zhen thereupon was moved to grief again and for long lost breath; the two men wept and could not master themselves, and went out in silent pity.
s0086.idiomatic: Zhen thereupon was moved to grief again and for long lost breath; the two men wept and could not master themselves, and went out in silent pity.

s0087.literal: Xu said to Keqing: "It is true—a house of filial piety has a filial son."
s0087.idiomatic: Xu said to Keqing, "It is true—a house of filial piety has a filial son."

s0088.literal: Keqing said: "The Xie house transmits utmost filial piety; which scholar-official does not look up to it? I fear he cannot rise—what then?"
s0088.idiomatic: Keqing said, "The Xie house transmits utmost filial piety; which scholar-official does not look up to it? I fear he cannot rise—what then?"

s0089.literal: Minister of Personnel Yao Cha of Wuxing was friendly with Zhen. When Zhen's illness grew critical, Cha went to visit him and asked about affairs after death. Zhen said: "This orphaned son has gathered calamity upon himself and will soon follow dust and earth.
s0089.idiomatic: Minister of personnel Yao Cha of Wuxing was friendly with Zhen. When Zhen's illness grew critical, Cha went to visit him and asked about affairs after death. Zhen said, "This orphaned son has gathered calamity upon himself and will soon follow dust and earth.

s0090.literal: My clansman Kai and the rest have roughly established themselves; I have already left a written instruction with them—this truly is not enough to bear up your thick virtue.
s0090.idiomatic: My clansman Kai and the rest have roughly established themselves; I have already left a written instruction with them—this truly is not enough to bear up your thick virtue.

s0091.literal: Today I am lost in gasping breath; the time cannot be shifted—let this be a final parting.
s0091.idiomatic: Today I am lost in gasping breath; the time cannot be shifted—let this be a final parting.

s0092.literal: My weak son is just six years old; his name is Jing, his style Yiren—the ties of feeling I cannot forget; I venture to entrust him to you."
s0092.idiomatic: My weak son is just six years old; his name is Jing, his style Yiren—the ties of feeling I cannot forget; I venture to entrust him to you."

s0093.literal: That night he died. An edict granted one hundred hu of grain for funeral expenses and thirty bolts of cloth.
s0093.idiomatic: That night he died. An edict granted one hundred hu of grain for funeral expenses and thirty bolts of cloth.

s0094.literal: Houzhu asked Cha: "What kin does Xie Zhen have?
s0094.idiomatic: Houzhu asked Cha, "What kin does Xie Zhen have?

s0095.literal: " Cha thereupon reported: "Zhen has one son, six years old."
s0095.idiomatic: Cha thereupon reported, "Zhen has one son, six years old."

s0096.literal: Thereupon an edict long supplied clothing and grain.
s0096.idiomatic: Thereupon an edict long supplied clothing and grain.

s0097.literal: Earlier, when Zhen's illness was critical, he left a written instruction telling his clansman Kai: "I in youth suffered harsh punishment; at fourteen I lost the shelter of kin outside, and at sixteen I met the calamity of Taiqing, drifting in exile and cut off from my state for more than twenty years.
s0097.idiomatic: Earlier, when Zhen's illness was critical, he left a written instruction telling his clansman Kai, "I in youth suffered harsh punishment; at fourteen I lost the shelter of kin outside, and at sixteen I met the calamity of Taiqing, drifting in exile and cut off from my state for more than twenty years.

s0098.literal: I cried to heaven and stamped the earth, and thus shared in the grief of all who feel; to return and serve, to guard my forefathers' tombs—for my portion that is enough.
s0098.idiomatic: I cried to heaven and stamped the earth, and thus shared in the grief of all who feel; to return and serve, to guard my forefathers' tombs—for my portion that is enough.

s0099.literal: I did not realize the court would gather up my emptiness and thinness and repeatedly raise me to clear ranks; even if I die utterly, there is nothing with which to repay.
s0099.idiomatic: I did not realize the court would gather up my emptiness and thinness and repeatedly raise me to clear ranks; even if I die utterly, there is nothing with which to repay.

s0100.literal: Now in the thorns of mourning the clepsydra's drip is nearly spent; I fold my hands and return—what is there to think much upon?
s0100.idiomatic: Now in the thorns of mourning the clepsydra's drip is nearly spent; I fold my hands and return—what is there to think much upon?
